_comment: Golden fixtures shared by every package. The device client, the dashboard and the attack harness all assert against these exact values, so an integration mistake surfaces as a data mismatch rather than a mystery. Firmware digests are never written here by hand: they are derived from `payload` with SHA-256, and scripts/build_fixtures.py writes the matching .bin files.

releases.payload:
SECUREOTA-FIRMWARE
model=RUH-SENSOR-01
version=1.2.0
build=release
note=baseline image the demo device ships with
releases.role: Baseline. The device starts here, and it is the target of the downgrade attack.

releases.payload:
SECUREOTA-FIRMWARE
model=RUH-SENSOR-01
version=1.3.0
build=release
note=withdrawn after CVE-2026-0001 in the TLS stack
releases.role: Published, then revoked. Devices must refuse it even though the bytes are genuine.

releases.payload:
SECUREOTA-FIRMWARE
model=RUH-SENSOR-01
version=1.4.0
build=release
note=current good release
releases.role: The good update. Happy path of the demo.
